glossary.def: Microsoft's open-source SDK for agents and graph workflows in C#, Python and Go, the successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen.
An ordinary agent pre-wired for long multi-step work: function invocation limits, todos, plan and execute modes, file memory, standing approvals, OpenTelemetry and optional compaction and looping.
The state object for one conversation: local history or a service conversation id, provider state keyed by `source_id`, and Harness state such as todos and pending approvals.
A `before_run` and `after_run` hook that injects instructions, messages, tools or middleware and learns from the exchange. Memory and retrieval are context providers.
A provider that loads and stores the transcript. Only one should load messages; others can capture audit copies.
Middleware around each model call. It runs once per model call, including every tool-loop iteration.
Middleware around each tool call, used for allow-lists, validation and timing.
A Harness rule that remembers an earlier 'always approve' answer for a tool, so later calls are approved without asking. It does not remove the tool's approval requirement.
Shrinking locally held history with strategies (tool-result collapse, summarization, sliding window, truncation) that act on atomic message groups. It has no effect on service-managed history.
A portable folder with `SKILL.md`, scripts and references (agentskills.io format) that an agent advertises cheaply and loads on demand.
A node in a workflow graph: a class with handlers or a function that receives typed messages, sends messages downstream and yields outputs.
One round of workflow execution in a Pregel-style model: collect messages, run target executors concurrently, wait at a barrier, then checkpoint and queue new messages.
A snapshot written at the end of each superstep with executor state, pending messages, pending requests and shared state. Storage is a trust boundary.
The workflow mechanism for sending a typed request out and waiting for a response. Pending requests are saved in checkpoints.
An orchestration where agents transfer control through tool calls in a mesh, and the receiving agent owns the task.
An orchestration with a central orchestrator that selects the next speaker over a shared conversation until a termination condition or round limit.
A group chat variant with a planning manager, task and progress ledgers, stall detection and replanning, based on Magentic-One.
A token returned by a background response that lets you poll for the result or resume an interrupted stream. A null token means done, failed or waiting for input.
Durable Task based hosting that persists agent sessions, checkpoints workflows and waits for human input without consuming compute. Beta in Python, preview in .NET.
An experimental Python control plane with fail-closed verdicts across agent, chat and function layers.

claims.text: Agent Framework 1.0 was announced on 2026-04-03 for .NET and Python with stable APIs and a commitment to long-term support.
Python agent-framework 1.21.0 was uploaded on 2026-10-08 and requires Python 3.10 or later.

The .NET core packages (Microsoft.Agents.AI and Abstractions, Workflows, Harness) are stable at 1.24.0 while Foundry, hosting, A2A, DevUI and AG-UI packages are preview; NuGet publish dates were not verified.
The Go SDK is in public preview and lacks declarative agents, RAG, CodeAct, functional workflows and a packaged Harness.
Semantic Kernel v1.x is supported for at least one year after Agent Framework GA, per the team blog of 2025-10-07; the earliest end of about 2027-04 is derived from the GA date.
HarnessAgent derives from AIAgent in .NET and create_harness_agent returns an Agent in Python, so the Harness is not a separate runtime.

Service-side ids such as OpenAI resp_* and conv_* are scoped to the API key or project and must not be treated as end-user authorization boundaries; map client ids to stored service ids and verify the user or tenant.
With agent middleware [A1, A2] and run middleware [R1, R2] the Python execution order is A1, A2, R1, R2, agent, R2, R1, A2, A1.
In .NET both runFunc and runStreamingFunc should be supplied; the Use(sharedFunc) overload cannot override output.
Python max_function_calls and max_duration_seconds default to None (unlimited), are checked after each model-requested batch and count approval wait time toward the duration.
disable_tool_auto_approval=True removes the Harness approval middleware but does not remove the approval requirement from a tool marked always_require.
A local approval response authorises a call only if it matches a pending request in the same AgentSession unless disable_approval_response_binding is set.

A skill description is limited to 1,024 characters, name to 64 characters; advertising costs about 100 tokens per skill; loading is recommended under 5,000 tokens; SKILL.md should stay under 500 lines.
In the Harness all three skill tools (load_skill, read_skill_resource, run_skill_script) require approval by default.
The todo provider exposes todos_add, todos_complete, todos_remove, todos_get_remaining and todos_get_all; the mode provider exposes mode_get and mode_set with plan and execute modes.
The plan-to-execute confirmation is instruction-level behaviour and not a tool-approval request.
Agent looping defaults to a maximum of 10 invocations, Python judge loops default to 5, and the loop stops when a tool approval is pending; the feature is experimental.
Only one history provider should use load_messages=True; audit providers use load_messages=False and store_context_messages=True.
require_per_service_call_history_persistence=True raises an error when the run is bound to a service-managed conversation, and the Harness requires per-call persistence.
In Python FileMemoryProvider derives its folder from the session id when scope is omitted, so sessions do not share files.
Compaction applies only to in-memory history and has no effect on Foundry agents, Responses with store on, or Copilot Studio; the Harness enables it only when token limits or a strategy are supplied.
Workflows run in supersteps (modified Pregel): all ready executors run concurrently, wait at a barrier, then messages for the next step are delivered.
In a switch-case edge group a predicate that raises fails the workflow rather than routing to the default target.
Since Python 1.13.0 (2026-07-30) workflows write an entry checkpoint before the first superstep and when request responses are delivered.
File, Cosmos and Foundry checkpoint stores in Python serialize non-JSON state with pickle behind a restricted unpickler and accept allowed_checkpoint_types entries in module:qualname form.
A rebuilt workflow must keep topology and executor identities; in .NET agents need a stable ChatClientAgentOptions.Id and an unchanged Name for checkpoint resume.

In Python an executor calls ctx.request_info and handles the answer in an @response_handler method; resume with workflow.run(responses=...); pending requests are saved in checkpoints and re-emitted on restore.
Middleware configured on a Python workflow-as-agent wrapper does not run, and wrapper context providers do not flow tools or middleware into workflow executors.
In sequential orchestration each agent receives the previous agent's whole conversation by default; chain_only_agent_responses=True passes only the reply; the last participant is the terminal output.
The default concurrent aggregator returns one AgentResponse with one assistant message per participant; with_aggregator replaces it.
Handoff supports only Agent with local tool execution, is interactive by default and its experimental autonomous mode defaults to 50 turns per agent in .NET.
With a custom BaseGroupChatOrchestrator the builder's max_rounds and termination_condition are ignored and all properties must be set on the orchestrator.
Magentic plan review is off by default in Python (enable_plan_review=False) and on by default in .NET (RequirePlanSignoff true); the docs say it is untested outside the Magentic-One design.
Background agents expose six tools, report task status running, completed, failed or lost, have no cancel tool and lose in-flight work on restart.
The Durable Extension pauses for human input without using compute or tokens and offers Azure Functions and bring-your-own-compute hosting; packages are Beta (Python) and preview (.NET).

Foundry hosted-agent default stores namespace state by platform user and sandbox session, use ETag conditions and expire sessions 30 days after the last write; hosting agent=workflow.as_agent() is deprecated in favour of workflow=.
Python instrumentation has been on by default since python-1.6.0 (2026-05-21), ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA defaults to false, and no exporter is installed automatically.
Python injects W3C trace context into params._meta only for MCP sessions the agent process opens, not for provider-hosted MCP tools or Foundry toolboxes.
AutoGen AssistantAgent is single-turn unless max_tool_iterations is raised, whereas the Agent Framework Agent is multi-turn by default.
